summary: US-A1: Customer accounts - register, sign in, sign out (the identity substrate)
description:
**As** a ticket buyer, **I want** an optional account I can create and sign in to,
**so that** my purchases can hang off an identity instead of only an order reference I have to keep.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** -

First slice of TKT-21. Guest checkout already works end to end (`buyer_pii`, `orders.guest_order_ref`,
and the retrieval page `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro`). What does not
exist is a *customer* - anywhere. This ticket creates one and nothing else: no order is attached to
it yet (TKT-221), there is no wallet (TKT-222) and no claiming (TKT-223).

**The decision this ticket owns:** where customer identity lives. ADR-042 put *staff* in catalog
because catalog owns organizers and staff administer an organizer. A customer administers nothing and
buys things, so the same reasoning does not transplant - it has to be re-run. That is a plan
decision with an ADR, not an implementation detail.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] An **ADR** records where customer identity lives and why, naming the rejected options with
  their reasons (a sixth service - already rejected once by ADR-042; the gateway - also already
  rejected; reusing `staff_accounts`; commerce; catalog). It states explicitly how the choice
  relates to ADR-002's five-service cut.
- [ ] A migration in the owning service adds customer accounts: the address in the buyer's original
  spelling for display, a normalized (trimmed, lower-cased) UNIQUE key that every lookup goes
  through, and a password hash. Mirror `staff_accounts`' two safety properties: a CHECK tripwire so
  a plaintext password written straight into the column fails loudly, and a **Down that refuses to
  drop a non-empty table**.
- [ ] Contract-declared **register** and **authenticate** operations (ADR-009; regen committed).
  The plan states, with reasoning, (a) which surface they live on and therefore how they are guarded
  per ADR-043, and (b) what registering with an already-registered address answers - account
  enumeration is a real disclosure and "answer success and mail the owner" is not available because
  **no email infrastructure exists in this repo**. Pick, and write down what the pick leaks.
- [ ] Authenticate makes **unknown account and wrong password indistinguishable** in the response,
  and does not skip the hash comparison when the account is unknown (a fast "no such account" is a
  timing oracle for which addresses are registered).
- [ ] The **storefront owns the session**, mirroring ADR-042's design: an opaque 256-bit token,
  HttpOnly, `SameSite=Lax`, an **absolute** TTL (not idle), a per-principal concurrent-session cap
  that is what actually bounds the session map, server-side destruction on sign-out (expiring the
  browser cookie only asks the browser to forget), and a cookie **path-scoped to the customer area
  rather than `/`** - the gateway serves the storefront, the scanner, `/admin/` and `/api/*` on one
  origin, so a `Path=/` cookie is attached to every API call and every scanner request.
- [ ] Every unsafe POST passes a **proxy-aware origin check**. Astro's `security.checkOrigin` cannot
  be used behind the gateway (TKT-105 / ADR-042): the Node adapter builds its URL from the
  container's own Host, so the comparison never matches and it 403s every POST.
- [ ] **The guest-first default is unchanged and provably so**: every existing storefront route stays
  reachable signed-out, no route gains a redirect-to-login, and checkout still needs no account.
- [ ] Signed-in pages answer `Cache-Control: no-store` and do **not** enter the minutes tier
  (`web/storefront/src/lib/page-tier.ts`).
- [ ] The storefront receives **no service credential** for this - or, if the chosen design needs
  one, the plan argues it explicitly and it is scoped to exactly these operations, never
  `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` and never `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`.
- [ ] Browser-submit verification (AGENTS.md): `make up`, then **submit** the new form(s) in a real browser — the smoke suite only renders, so the whole SSR-rejects-the-write class (origin check, base path, redirect, CSP) is invisible to it. Evidence in the PR.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** password reset, email verification, magic links, OAuth/SSO (there is no mail path in
this repo) - attaching an order to an account (TKT-221) - the wallet (TKT-222) - claiming a guest
order (TKT-223) - rate limiting the public sign-in/registration surface (TKT-195 is the back-office
equivalent; the storefront one is a follow-up this ticket must file, not solve).

objective.note: A buyer can create an account and sign in; nothing else changes. The identity exists for TKT-221/222/223 to hang off.

scope.note: Accounts table + register/authenticate + storefront session and forms + an ADR. No order touches an account in this ticket.

uncertainties.note: (a) which service owns customer accounts - the ADR is an AC, not an assumption; (b) public-contract operation vs guarded surface, which ADR-043 decides once (a) is answered; (c) what a duplicate registration answers, an explicit named trade-off in the ACs. None of the three blocks starting: each is a plan decision with the constraints already written down.

dependencies.note: None. Guest checkout, the gateway route table and the storefront shell all exist.

approach.note: Mirror the shipped staff-auth stack: catalog 0015 + staff.go + api/staff.go for the service half, web/backoffice/src/lib/{session,gate}.ts + middleware.ts for the session half. The test seams are the same ones those use (gate.ts extracted from middleware.ts precisely because astro:middleware does not resolve under vitest).

first_slice.note: Nothing in this epic can be demonstrated without a customer that exists and can prove who it is.

success.note: Deterministic: register, authenticate, refuse, sign out, plus a browser submit of each form.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages - it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it.

governingAdrs.why: Cuts the system at five services + a stateless gateway. Customer accounts must land inside an existing service or the deviation is recorded as an ADR - ADR-042 rejected a sixth identity service and rejected giving the gateway a database.

The precedent AND its reasoning: staff accounts in catalog because catalog owns organizers; the SSR app owns the session, not the service; sessions in-process and unpersisted; per-principal session cap is what bounds the map; the cookie is path-scoped because storefront/scanner/admin/api share ONE origin. It also records that Astro's `security.checkOrigin` CANNOT be turned on behind the gateway (the Node adapter compares against the container Host) - a proxy-aware origin check replaces it.

The rule for where a guard lives: declared `security:` guards operations in a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline `X-Internal-Token` check guards its INTERNAL surface. Commerce's 404-on-internal is load-bearing (it matches the gateway edge-deny), not cargo. Whichever surface customer register/authenticate lands on, this decides how it is guarded.
Contract-first: any new operation is declared in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code is committed before the gate runs.
Migrations run OUT-OF-BAND - the binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates. Any new table follows this.

Catalog public read cache / the minutes tier. Per-customer HTML is never cacheable: signed-in pages must answer `Cache-Control: no-store` and must not enter `web/storefront/src/lib/page-tier.ts`'s CACHED_PAGE set.

Name the adversary before claiming a security property. 'A customer cannot see another customer's orders' means an unauthenticated or differently-authenticated HTTP caller - it says nothing about anyone with database access.
Response drift fails closed: a handler whose response does not match the declared schema is refused, so a new operation's schema must actually match what the handler writes.

reference.summary: BLAST RADIUS - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` (compose.yaml `&go-env` anchor) is ONE shared value across all five Go services: whatever holds it can call commerce's /internal/orders/{id}/refunds, inventory's /internal/operational-holds and /internal/slots/{id}/capacity-adjustments, and access's refund surface. The storefront must NEVER receive it.
BLAST RADIUS - `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` opens commerce's staff refund (money-moving). Held today only by the back office. The storefront must NEVER receive it.

The storefront container today has exactly ONE env var: `GATEWAY_URL`. It holds no credential of any kind and serves anonymous internet traffic. Any design that hands it a token is a new trust decision that must be argued, not assumed.

Precedent to mirror, not to copy blindly: staff sign-in is catalog `staff_accounts` (migration 0015, bcrypt + tripwire CHECK + non-empty-Down refusal), `services/catalog/internal/store/staff.go`, `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go`; the SESSION lives in the back-office Astro process (`web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`, `gate.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`) - opaque 256-bit token, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, absolute 8h TTL, per-principal cap of 5, cookie scoped to `/admin` NOT `/`.
